objects.name: Compile scientific data into visible mechanics
objects.notes:
STATEMENT: Pinned CoolProp surface-tension correlations can bind through the creature graph to a triangulated, pinned-boundary interface whose native equilibrium geometry supplies its rendered light.
PREDICTION: At fixed geometry reaction and area energy scale with source gamma; under equal load ethanol deflects more than water; releasing load returns a flat surface; native analytic gradient matches a finite-difference energy oracle; imported temperature outside declared bounds refuses compilation.
FALSIFIERS: changed source bytes accepted under old hashes; missing graph material edge compiles; collinear anchors compile; derivative relative error > 1e-5; force-balance residual > 1e-7 N at a settled state; release depth > 1e-7 m; source gamma change has no mechanical effect; observed frame remains pixel-identical across loaded/unloaded states; rendered mesh differs from accepted native state. Numerical tolerances are verification bounds, not fitted physical parameters.
MODEL: U = gamma sum(A_triangle) + F sum(w_i h_i), with the frame normal pointing upward and positive F pressing down. Every interior height is a free coordinate; rim heights are fixed. Minimize this convex height-field area energy using Newton-CG and energy-decreasing backtracking. No inertia or elapsed-time interpretation. Surface tension correlation gamma(T)=sum(a_i(1-T/Tc)^n_i) comes from pinned upstream JSON. Pure liquid-vapor equilibrium coefficient; virtual zero-gravity, equal-pressure, fixed-rim interface. No claim of skin law, full liquid flow, or biological creature qualification.
GEOMETRY: three non-collinear anchors define local plane; dimensions, mesh resolution, probe footprint and imposed load are explicitly authored apparatus settings. No material property is chosen for appearance. Native C++ runs mechanics; Python downloads/imports/compiles once only; the existing Vulkan engine renders accepted vertices.
